messages:
ben: Quick follow-up on the iterator surface discussion — we need a concrete proposal for how pull vs push semantics interact with retries, resume tokens, and transport choices across py/ts/go. TL;DR: two surfaces or one unified contract?

emma: Short answer: keep ergonomic language-native surfaces but unify the guarantees and signal semantics. We shouldn't leak transport details to app devs.

rishi: Agree. From Go's POV we usually expose a channel (<-chan Item) not an iterator. But we can map semantics: channel reads == iterator next. Important: resume semantics must be explicit and idempotent.

laura: Two concrete resume token options we talked about earlier: 1) Opaque blob (base64) that encodes server state, 2) Deterministic cursor (seq number + model shard). Tradeoffs: opaque is future-proof but opaque tokens mean server can change internals without client changes. Deterministic cursor is smaller but couples client/server.

mike: Also consider payload size of resume tokens: clients on mobile/browsers prefer small tokens. Opaque tokens can be compressed but often grow with metadata.

emma: For retries we need a single source-of-truth: introduce a `request_id` + `resume_token`. Behavior: server should treat same request_id as idempotent for a short TTL and use resume_token to continue streaming from last acked item. This avoids duplicate processing.

ben: Sample request shape I sketched:

```
POST /v1/messages/list
{
  "page_size": 128,
  "resume_token": "<base64>",
  "request_id": "uuid-v4"
}
```

Responses for unary pagination: `items[], next_resume_token`. For streaming (http2 grpc-web) yield items and periodically send `resume_token` checkpoints as metadata frames.

rishi: On the transport side: prefer HTTP/2 server-streaming when available because it lets us push checkpoints without extra RTT. Fallbacks: unary paginated endpoints for browsers (CORS + gRPC-web issues) and WebSocket streaming as an opt-in for long-lived mobile sessions.

laura: Important tradeoff: server-side state vs stateless resume. If resume_token encodes server cursor only, then server maintains minimal ephemeral state (tombstones). If token references a server-side ephemeral session id, you need session GC and more operational complexity. I'd prefer stateless tokens at first.

mike: How do we surface partial duplicates to the user? If a client reconnects and receives last N items again we should provide at-least-once but mark items with `id` so apps can dedupe. That way we avoid strong exactly-once semantics which are expensive.

emma: Exactly. Contract proposal:
- Delivery: at-least-once.
- Idempotency: each item includes stable `item_id` (string) and `seq` (int64) when available.
- Resume: server returns `resume_token` representing the next-seq point; clients can pass token to resume.
- Request id for dedup of client-side retries, server honors within a short TTL (e.g., 60s).

ben: Language surface sketches:
- Python: `async for item in client.list_messages(..., resume_token=None, request_id=None):`
- TS: `for await (const item of client.listMessages(...)) {}` with `client.listMessages.options.resumeToken` available on the iterator object for manual checkpoints.
- Go: `ch := client.ListMessages(ctx, opts); for item := range ch {}` and `opts.ResumeToken`/`opts.RequestID` to resume.

rishi: Need to be careful with memory: streaming implementations keeping large internal buffers so that replay is cheap will blow up memory with big page_size. Suggest default page_size=64 and advise users to tune. Also we should offer a `prefetch` knob per language.

laura: Testing matrix: we have to validate across transports: grpc streaming, http2 stream, unary paginated, and websockets. Also validate for partial checkpoint emission frequency (every N items or time window).

mike: Security note: resume_token should be HMAC-signed to prevent tampering if we put any customer-visible offsets inside. If opaque base64 includes tenant/shard ids we must sign + rotate keys.

emma: Rollout plan:
1) Implement server unary paginated with resume_token and request_id.
2) Ship language adapters that map to idiomatic surfaces (py/ts/go) behind a feature flag `iter-unify-v1`.
3) Optionally implement server-streaming transport later with identical checkpoint semantics.

ben: Canary: enable flag for 10% of orgs and 5 pilot customers on dedicated infra. Monitor: duplicate delivery rate, resume success rate, average resume token size, and memory usage per stream.

rishi: One last nuance: if we allow `resume_token=null` as start-of-stream, servers should keep logical monotonic seqs even if internal compaction happens. If compaction removes old seqs then tokens referencing removed seqs should return a helpful `410 GONE` with `new_resume_token` suggestion.

laura: +1 for helpful error semantics. Also add a `resumption_hint` field in errors so SDKs can auto-retry with suggested token.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag infra rollout plan created (#FF-1234).

ben: Action items: emma to draft explicit contract doc (fields + code samples) by EOD Wednesday; rishi to prototype Go channel adapter; laura to spec token format and HMAC rotation; mike to run perf sims on token size vs page_size. I'll own rollout checklist and telemetry. Thanks all :thumbsup:
